Only raise CRITICAL when evaluation is supported **and** the list is empty.\\n\\n## 3. Access to many models is enabled by default with the right AWS Marketplace permissions; the usual causes are a missing `aws-marketplace` permission for the first (subscribing) call, an IAM or SCP deny, the Anthropic first-time-use form for Anthropic models earlier than Claude Opus 4.7, or additional account-level access the model needs ([model access](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-access.html)). Counted only here, not in `Invocations`, `InvocationClientErrors` or `InvocationServerErrors`, so an error total or a per-code reconciliation must add this metric | Sum |\\n| `InputTokenCount` | Count | Tokens in the input/prompt | Sum, Average |\\n| `OutputTokenCount` | Count | Tokens generated in the output | Sum, Average |\\n| `OutputImageCount` | Count | Images generated (image models) | Sum |\\n| `TimeToFirstToken` | Milliseconds | Latency to first streamed token (streaming calls) | Average, p90 |\\n| `EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage` | Count | Estimated tokens-per-minute quota consumption across `Converse`, `ConverseStream`, `InvokeModel` and `InvokeModelWithResponseStream`; an approximation in tokens, not a percentage. There is no `EstimatedQuotaConsumption` metric | Sum |\\n\\nToken metrics (`InputTokenCount` / `OutputTokenCount`) are the primary signal for cost analysis \u2014 see `cost-analysis.md`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## AWS/Bedrock/Guardrails \u2014 guardrail metrics\\n\\nNamespace: `AWS/Bedrock/Guardrails`. Series that carry `GuardrailArn` carry only `GuardrailArn` + `GuardrailVersion`; series with `Operation`, `GuardrailContentSource` or `GuardrailPolicyType` carry no `GuardrailArn`, so they are account-wide, and the `Operation` series also counts inline evaluations (measured on `Converse`), not only standalone `ApplyGuardrail` calls. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/monitoring-guardrails-cw-metrics.html\\n\\n| Metric | Meaning |\\n|---|---|\\n| `InvocationsIntervened` | AWS: \"Number of invocations where the guardrails intervened\". Measured on non-streaming inline `Converse`, one model, one Region, it counted guardrail evaluations, not model calls: an allowed call counted 2, a call blocked at the input counted 1 |\\n| `InvocationLatency` | AWS defines it as the time from when a request is sent to when the last token is received. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/monitoring-agents-cw-metrics.html\\n\\n| Metric | Meaning |\\n|---|---|\\n| `InvocationCount` / `Invocations` | Number of `InvokeAgent` calls |\\n| `InvocationLatency` | Agent end-to-end orchestration latency |\\n| `InvocationClientErrors` | Client-side (4xx) errors on agent invoke |\\n| `InvocationServerErrors` | Server-side (5xx) errors on agent invoke |\\n| `InvocationThrottles` | Throttled agent invocations |\\n\\nZero invocation data over a long window is the signal for the idle-agent check (LLM-AGT-004).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Knowledge Base signals\\n\\nKnowledge Base ingestion health is read primarily from the data-plane/control-plane APIs (the per-job `statistics` in `bedrock:ListIngestionJobs`), not a dedicated CloudWatch namespace.
